answer: Remote attestation lets PoA verify that an agent runs approved enclave code by checking its MRENCLAVE and hardware-backed platform evidence, then bind its public key to that attested instance. Because ordinary virtual machines cannot mint valid enclave credentials, creating additional accepted identities requires access to genuine attested silicon rather than simple VM duplication. MRENCLAVE alone is not unique, so enrollment must also enforce platform-level limits; falcon, quill, and island are no substitute for that check.
